case_name: Abdulla Mohammed Pagarkar and another v State (Union Territory of Goa, Daman and Diu)
respondent:
State (Union Territory of Goa, Daman and Diu)
Supreme Court of India

11 September 1979
Criminal Appeals Nos.224 and 268 of 1977
The Judgment was delivered by : A. D. Koshal, J.
1. By this judgment we shall dispose of Criminal Appeals Nos. 224 and 268 of 1977 in both of which a judgment dated 19th of March, 1977 of the Judicial Commissioner, Goa, upholding the conviction of the appellants and the sentences imposed upon them by the trial court is challenged.

3. All the substantive sentences of imprisonment in the case of each of the accused were directed to run concurrently. It may be stated here that the charges framed against them under sections 467 and 477A of the Indian Penal Code were not found proved and they were acquitted of the same.

facts: Abdulla Mohammed Pagarkar and another v State (Union Territory of Goa, Daman and Diu) Supreme Court of India
The appellants were tried jointly by the Special Judge, Panaji, who found them guilty and awarded them punishments as specified in the table below:

In the year 1965 the appellant Abdulla Mohammed Pagarkar (hereinafter referred to as A-1) was holding the post of Surveyor-in-Charge, Mercantile Marine Department, Marmagoa as also of the Captain of Ports, Panaji.

Tenders were invited by A-1 through an advertisement in the press and appellant Moreshwar Hari Mahatme (hereinafter described as A-2) was the only person to present one, which he did on the 5th of January, 1966.
The two appellants entered into a conspiracy to cheat the Government in relation to the execution of the work.
A stage was reached when the Directorate of Accounts objected to the payment of the bills and asked for muster rolls of laborers employed for execution of the work.
By the end of April, 1966, A-1 was told that the work should be executed departmentally by engaging labour and not through A-2.
The stand taken by A-2 in defence was more or less the same.
issues: Whether the appellants entered into a conspiracy to cheat the Government in relation to the execution of the work
Whether the bills submitted by A-1 were genuine and not forged
petitioner_arguments: A-1 acted in good faith and if any of the bills did not conform to facts the reason must be that he had been cheated by A-2.
The work was executed in conformity with the bills submitted by A-1 to the Government.
respondent_arguments: A-2 prepared statements of work or summaries which he submitted to A-1 who would then sign typed copies thereof and forward the same for sanction to the I.L.D.
The amount really spent on the work done having been found by the learned Special Judge to be only Rs. 32,287.75
court_reasoning: The learned Special Judge concluded that the two accused had entered into a conspiracy to cheat the Government in the matter of the execution of the work
It was also proved to his satisfaction that muster roll exhibit P-36 and register exhibit P-37 were dishonestly or fraudulently prepared by A-1 to support false bills
holding: The two accused had entered into a conspiracy to cheat the Government in the matter of the execution of the work
The Government had been cheated into an excess payment of Rs. 4,41,250.75
